chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever bequeaths one-third of his estate and is then killed by mistake,' he said: 'One-third of his blood money (diyah) is included in his bequest.'

key_terms.دِيَة: blood money / compensation for accidental death

ai.seo_question: How is blood money distributed if the deceased had already bequeathed one-third of their estate?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal status of blood money (*diyah*) in the context of bequests, specifically ruling that one-third of the *diyah* falls under the testator's designated one-third share for bequests rather than the full amount. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that *diyah* is treated as part of the estate's assets subject to the deceased's final wishes, provided it does not exceed the standard one-third limit for bequests. It underscores the precision in Shia inheritance law regarding how different types of wealth are categorized and distributed upon death.
